title: Pip and the Rainy-Day Map

premise.want: Pip wants Bea to find his hidden paper star using a map.
premise.why_now: Rain has moved their treasure hunt indoors.
premise.stakes: The game will stop being fun if Bea cannot understand the clues.
premise.obstacle: Pip draws the route he remembers without any landmarks Bea can recognize.
premise.turn: Pip notices a raindrop passing recognizable things and tests a revised map from Bea’s starting place.
premise.ending: Bea finds the star and begins a new map for Pip.
premise.theme: An idea becomes shareable when we make room for another person’s view.

cast.want: Pip wants Bea to find his hidden paper star using a map.
cast.need: To test his directions from Bea’s starting place.
cast.starting_state: Certain his drawing says everything he knows.
cast.ending_state: Proud of a map Bea can follow and ready to try her game.

cast.need: Clues she can connect to the room.
cast.ending_state: Successful and eager to invent the next map.

beats.action: Pip hides a paper star in a spare boot and gives Bea a map drawn as one curly line.
beats.consequence: Bea starts from the door, eager to follow the line.
beats.emotion: Pip feels excited; Bea is curious.
beats.visual_reveal: The reader sees the star tucked inside the left spare blue boot, but Bea is facing the map.
beats.text: Rain tapped the window. Pip had a plan. He tucked a paper star into a boot and drew Bea a treasure map. One long, curly line. “Follow this!”

beats.action: Bea follows the curly line as far as the table, then cannot tell which way to turn.
beats.consequence: Pip learns that his remembered route is not visible to Bea.
beats.emotion: Bea is puzzled; Pip is surprised.
beats.visual_reveal: The same curl could lead around either side of the round table.
beats.text: Bea reached the table. Then where? Pip tapped the curl. “I know where it goes.” Bea turned the map sideways. “I don’t.”

beats.action: Pip covers the line with arrows without adding room landmarks. Bea follows an arrow toward the umbrella stand.
beats.consequence: The arrows still do not tell Bea where she is; the hunt stops.
beats.emotion: Pip feels disappointed and folds his ears down; Bea waits without blaming him.
beats.visual_reveal: An umbrella tip pokes above Bea like a question mark; the star remains hidden in the boot.
beats.text: “More arrows!” said Pip. Bea tried again. She reached an umbrella. No star. Pip’s ears drooped. He had made the map bigger. Why wasn’t the game better?

beats.action: Pip pauses at the window and watches a raindrop pass a stuck leaf and a small snail outside.
beats.consequence: He notices that recognizable things make a route easier to describe.
beats.emotion: Pip feels quiet first, then interested enough to try again.
beats.visual_reveal: A single raindrop passes two clear reference points; the snail has its own slow journey along the outside ledge.
beats.text: Pip sat quietly. A raindrop slipped down the glass: past a leaf, past a snail. Pip looked from the window to the room. “My map needs things to look for.”

dialogue.text: My map needs things to look for.

beats.action: Pip draws the table, umbrella stand and two boots, then walks the route from Bea’s starting place while checking each picture.
beats.consequence: The revised route works from the doorway. He gives Bea the tested map.
beats.emotion: Pip feels hopeful; Bea is ready for another turn.
beats.visual_reveal: Map and room align in an overhead view. A star symbol points into the left spare blue boot.
beats.text: He drew the table. The umbrella. Two boots. Landmarks! Pip tried the map from Bea’s starting place. Now each picture matched. “Your turn.” Can you spot the last landmark?

beats.action: Bea follows the landmarks and lifts the paper star from the left boot, then asks for a fresh sheet to make a map for Pip.
beats.consequence: The treasure hunt succeeds, and the friends swap roles for another game.
beats.visual_reveal: Bea holds the star, both boots are visible, and the snail has finally reached the end of the outside ledge.
beats.text: Past the table. Past the umbrella. There were the boots! Bea reached inside. A star! “Another map?” asked Pip. “Yes,” said Bea. “This time, you follow me.” Rain tapped. Pencils scratched.

dialogue.text: Yes. This time, you follow me.

purpose.intent: Turn a small misunderstanding between friends into a satisfying, playful discovery.
purpose.teaching_goal: Recognize that familiar landmarks make a map easier to follow.
purpose.lesson: When a friend is puzzled, try changing the explanation and testing it together.
purpose.delivery: The curly line fails in beat-02; extra arrows still fail in beat-03. After feeling disappointed, Pip notices visible reference points in beat-04. He draws and tests landmarks in beat-05. Bea uses them independently in beat-06. The narrator does not state a rule or claim a measured learning outcome.
